title.narrative: OC10

description.narrative: Dedicated platform for exchange of digitised archive material developed and regularly accessed by various PSMs in the region.

comment.narrative: Exchange platform is established and functioning material is uploaded staff are trained

35 technical and management staff of PSMs have been trained and gained knowledge about the process of digitalization of archive material metadata collection and the importance of archives for everyday multimedia production and promotion of PSM brand on all platforms.The final list of metadata for 884 hours of archive content representing 1302 items was prepared for regional platform for exchange of digitized archive material and distributed to all six PSMs archive departmentsAll 6 PSMs appointed staff members in charge of the archive platform and they all gained access and the opportunity to work with the platform The platform for the exchange of archive material housing the prepared material from all six PSMs has been developed tested and will be launched before the end of the project implementation period.The work was presented at the Western Balkans regional archive workshop held within the FIATIFTA WorldConference 2019 in October in Dubrovnik generating significant interest by the international community.Six PSMs have signed a declaration underlining the importance of the platform and their willingness and interest to take over the ownership of the platform. The Declaration statesWe as the group of 6 PSM from the Western Balkans beneficiaries of the Project Technical Assistance to PSMs in Western Balkans express our willingness to continue our cooperation on the archive preservation and digitalisation. We see the provided solution of the online archive exchange platform as the central future tool and a search engine for our cooperation on the regional and European level. It will significantly reduce time and efforts for research and production and on the other hand provide access to an important part of our cultural heritage. There is a huge potential to open new markets and connect even more archives than currently present in the group. We are willing as a group to consider the future ownership of the platform including its legal and financial implications.

title.narrative: OC1

description.narrative: Fundamental principles for PSM funding are agreed along the following lines:Funding should not be dependent on the state budget,The size of the funding should be fixed over a longer timeframe, thereby minimising the possibilities for political interference Funding models should make PSM accountable to their audience on an individual levelFunding should be administered by the PSM and should not be fettered by state rules whilst also being transparent and accountable to the publicThe collection mechanism is ensured and ultimately guaranteed by the state There is an increase in the number of PSMs which apply these principles, adjusted to the local context.

comment.narrative: 2017Albania Has a wellfunctioning licence fee systemBosnia and Herzegovina Major collection problems for the licence fee BHRT is piloting an initiative to collect the licence fee via electricity billsKosovo RTK is currently funded by the state budget plans to reintroduce the licence fee are being blockedFYR Macedonia The broadcast tax is very expensive to collect and MRT has no control over the collectionMontenegro Funded by the state budgetSerbia The licence fee of 500 dinars has been replaced by a 150dinar tax. The shortfall is covered by the State

Sustainable model is developed and agreed on a regional level. On a national level the following changes are notedBosnia and Herzegovina The BHRT collection initiative is supported by the project and replicated if successfulKosovo Advocacy work breaks the current deadlock and the licence fee is reintroducedFYR Macedonia New funding model is agreed advocacy over adoption is providedSerbia and Montenegro Awareness of the weaknesses of their models is raised amongst the public and public officials creating impetus for reform2020Assessment reports are reviewed in light of Covid192021Plans for postCovid funding changes basedon assessmentreports are discussed and presented to ministries government representatives and parliamentary committees2022Progress made in implementation of common funding principles PSMs undertake public diplomacy campaigns in line with European best practice.By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs have moved in the direction of the recommendations with regard to the election of governing bodies On a national level the targets areAlbania Election process clarified and Code acceptedBosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo Code acceptedFYR Macedonia Improvements in the election composition and functioning of the Council in line with the Code are mooted and gain the approval of key stakeholdersMontenegro The appointment process is addressed and the recommendations of the Code shape policy discussions on this issueSerbia Awareness is raised of the risk of politicisation within REM impacting on the independence of the Steering Board 2021Annual analysisassessment of existingPSM governancepractice and itscompliance with regionalPSM governanceprinciples202122Assessment reportspublicly discussed andpresented to government relevant ministries andparliamentarycommittees in 6countries2022By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs are taking steps to implement common principles on governance and with regard to the election of governing bodiesPSMs undertake public diplomacy campaigns in line with European best practice.

The principles were agreed and some changes have been introduced. Common Funding Principles for Public Service Media in the Western Balkans agreed upon by 50 stakeholders from the six countries at the regional conference in Sarajevo May 2019 including Guidelines for Implementation of Common Funding Principles for Public Service Media in the Western Balkans.Six national assessment groups were established and following continuous monitoring six national assessment reports on PSM funding were produced. Updated final assessment reports are being publicly launched at a regional conference on 5 July 2022. The reports set out concrete recommendations for change including legislative proposals to enhance sustainable funding and independence. These documents are valuable tools for various legislative initiatives in all WB countries and will be used in follow up support and public advocacy activities with relevant stakeholders and decision makers in all 6 WB countries.Awareness was raised among decisionmakers during six national discussions attended by 180 stakeholders. Significant publicity of these roundtable events contributed to a better understanding of European standards and best practices in PSM funding.Public advocacy program conducted in six countries during the project implementation period with direct interventions in Montenegrin and Kosovo legislative process including implementation challenges in North Macedonia and Bosnia Regional principles for PSM funding in Western Balkans are serving as a reference point for public discussion and ongoing legislative deliberations in Western Balkans countries

title.narrative: OC2

description.narrative: Code of Conduct developed which embraces the following recommendations:Nominating organisations include freedom of speech, human rights, journalists and media associations as well as judges, universities etc. They exclude political functionaries and create efficient safeguards against direct interference from public authorities, parliament and government Number of nominated candidates: the nominating organisations choose their candidates through a competitive public process and agree on a list with the number of candidates necessary for the governing body. A proper gender balance is observedRequirements for the proposed candidates: exclusion of potential economic conflicts of interest and of active political engagement and conflicts of interest. Requirements for educational qualifications and specific professional experience are related to the work in the governing body.Parliamentary validation: a parliamentary committee or other delegated body, such as the regulatory authority, validates the list of nominated candidates ensuring compliance with the requirements and putting the list to a parliamentary vote

comment.narrative: In all countries the process of election of members for the governing body is defined in laws bylaws or regulations. However no code of conduct minimising the risk for politicisation of the process has been agreed as a benchmark for the future election of members of the governing bodies.2017Albania Lacks a clear description of the process and consequently the election of members is politicisedBosnia and Herzegovina Politicians have significant influence over the nomination and dismissal of Board membersKosovo Board members are appointed by the Kosovo AssemblyFYR Macedonia There is room for improvement in the election composition and functioning of the CouncilMontenegro There is room for improvement in the legislation as political pressures are noted during the appointment processSerbia REM plays a key role in the election of the Steering Board REM members are appointed by the government

By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs have moved in the direction of the recommendations with regard to the election of governing bodies On a national level the targets areAlbania Election process clarified and Code acceptedBosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo Code acceptedFYR Macedonia Improvements in the election composition and functioning of the Council in line with the Code are mooted and gain the approval of key stakeholdersMontenegro The appointment process is addressed and the recommendations of the Code shape policy discussions on this issueSerbia Awareness is raised of the risk of politicisation within REM impacting on the independence of the Steering Board 2021Annual analysis assessment of existing PSM governance practice and its compliance with regional PSM governance principles202122Assessment reports publicly discussed and presented to government relevant ministries and parliamentary committees in 6 countries2022By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs are taking steps to implement common principles on governance and with regard to the election of governing bodiesPSMs undertake public diplomacy campaigns in line with European best practice.

Progress was made but there remains too much political interference in the process. Common principles were agreed and some steps have been taken towards implementation.Common Principles on PSM GovernanceSupervision in the Western Balkans agreed upon and adopted by project stakeholders at the Belgrade regional conference February 2020.Six regional debates organized and public discussion initiated with more than 180 stakeholders directly involved.National assessment groups set up and countryspecific reports produced with concrete recommendations for PSM governance Awareness raised among stakeholders on the necessity to clearly separate PSM powers among management and governing structures. Regionally agreed common principles documents for PSM funding and governance formally accepted by the EUMontenegro Stabilisation and Association Parliamentary Committee SAPC held in Podgorica in February 2020. Significant publicity produced and public advocacy programs conducted in 6 countries during the project implementation period. Regional principles for PSM governance in Western Balkans are serving as a reference point for public discussion and ongoing legislative deliberations in six Western Balkans countries.

However no code of conduct minimising the risk for politicisation of the process has been agreed as a benchmark for the future election of members of the governing bodies.2017Albania Lacks a clear description of the process and consequently the election of members is politicisedBosnia and Herzegovina Politicians have significant influence over the nomination and dismissal of Board membersKosovo Board members are appointed by the Kosovo AssemblyFYR Macedonia There is room for improvement in the election composition and functioning of the CouncilMontenegro There is room for improvement in the legislation as political pressures are noted during the appointment processSerbia REM plays a key role in the election of the Steering Board REM members are appointed by the government

By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs have moved in the direction of the recommendations with regard to the election of governing bodies On a national level the targets areAlbania Election process clarified and Code acceptedBosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo Code acceptedFYR Macedonia Improvements in the election composition and functioning of the Council in line with the Code are mooted and gain the approval of key stakeholdersMontenegro The appointment process is addressed and the recommendations of the Code shape policy discussions on this issueSerbia Awareness is raised of the risk of politicisation within REM impacting on the independence of the Steering Board 2021Annual analysis assessment of existing PSM governance practice and its compliance with regional PSM governance principles202122Assessment reports publicly discussed and presented to government relevant ministries and parliamentary committees in 6 countries2022By the end of the project a majority of the PSMs are taking steps to implement common principles on governance and with regard to the election of governing bodiesPSMs undertake public diplomacy campaigns in line with European best practice.

Progress was made but there remains too much political interference in the process. Common principles were agreed and some steps have been taken towards implementation.Common Principles on PSM GovernanceSupervision in the Western Balkans agreed upon and adopted by project stakeholders at the Belgrade regional conference February 2020.Six regional debates organized and public discussion initiated with more than 180 stakeholders directly involved.National assessment groups set up and countryspecific reports produced with concrete recommendations for PSM governance Awareness raised among stakeholders on the necessity to clearly separate PSM powers among management and governing structures. Regionally agreed common principles documents for PSM funding and governance formally accepted by the EUMontenegro Stabilisation and Association Parliamentary Committee SAPC held in Podgorica in February 2020. Significant publicity produced and public advocacy programs conducted in 6 countries during the project implementation period. Regional principles for PSM governance in Western Balkans are serving as a reference point for public discussion and ongoing legislative deliberations in six Western Balkans countries.

title.narrative: OC3

description.narrative: Code of conduct for editorial guidelines and complaints mechanism are agreed; existing editorial guidelines are updated to incorporate issues of gender equality, social media, UGC etc

comment.narrative: All six PSMs have updated guidelinescodes of conductMore than 100 journalists and editorial staff gained better knowledge of the content of its PSMs editorial guidelines and the way of its effective implementation and daily usage in practice. All six PSMs agreed to and signed the joint framework for editorial and ethical guidelines and the list of recommendations for improved implementation. June 2019. With the declaration all 6 PSMs committed themselves tooTo adopt editorial guidelines that would ideally include and detail PSM values ethical principles issues practices and proceduresoTo update periodically these editorial guidelines in order to address emerging issues or dilemmasoTo do so drawing up and updating in consultation with journalists to ease appropriation of common standards in the newsroomoTo organize regular newsroom meetings and trainings to share ethical problems behavior and standardsoTo mentor young journalists to generalize ethical behavioroTo capitalize in the long term on experienced journalists interested in ethicsoTo develop whenever possible ethical support to journalists such as a head of ethics in the newsroom or a newsombudsman.At RTSH RTK and RTCG journalists developed processes for implementing guidelines in daily activity.BHRT developed updated guidelines as a result of national workshopsAt MRT journalists have been trained on how to implement guidelines in a politically challenging environmentAt RTS a code of conduct for employees and editorial guidelines was developed. The national coaching ensured wider dissemination and ownership of the editorial guidelines by involving both journalistic and editorial staff and using a bottomup approach. Awareness was raised on the need for and effective use of complaints mechanisms and best practices were shared by European media.Tailormade stepbystep road map and timeline for each PSM on introducing complaints mechanisms agreed in each of the six Western Balkans countries.RTCG appointed a new Ombudsperson and the project provided expertise via Ombudsperson of RTV Slovenia to strengthen their work. She gained knowledge of the relations and necessary rules for the relations of Ombudsman with main stakeholders such as editorial offices management board and viewers and listeners.

title.narrative: OC4: Jointly developed strategies and implemented action plans for setting up integrated newsrooms and other multiplatform production and distribution media: radio, television, mobile and onlinevernment are more efficientn of Strategy Document. of CYWD.

description.narrative: OC4: Jointly developed strategies and implemented action plans for setting up integrated newsrooms and other multiplatform production and distribution media: radio, television, mobile and online

title.narrative: OC4

description.narrative: Degree and detail to which the strategy and plans for integrated newsrooms are agreed and the number of PSMs in which they are implemented

comment.narrative: 2017Only the broadcasters in Bosnia and Herzegovina have introduced the technical and personnel changes necessary to support the transition to an integrated newsroom

2021In all six countries implementation strategies are agreed and working procedures adopted with the introduction of new newsroom positions like social media content producer mobile journalists expert for data visualization etc.The plans are presented to senior management and in the event of a positive response implementation processes begin.80 journalists trained in social media production data visualisation mobile journalism

Significant steps were taken towards integration of newsrooms from training to new newsroom structures to investment in technology to developing new production processes and the physical relocation of staff and departments.Achieved results and impact Awareness raised of benefits of and requirements for developing integrated newsrooms as a result of study visit to YLE Finland.News and production staff of all six PSMs have been trained how to better organize daily planning and manage production resources to coordinate news teams across platforms in order to achieve maximum efficiency and improve online output.Six tailored national action plans for setting up integrated newsrooms and multiplatform production and distribution radio television mobile and online have been produced and presented to management. Common to all actions plans is oIdentifying the weaknesses within existing teams and the training needs for journalistsoIntroducing policies which ensure unified approaches and a robust editorial frameworkoIntroducing management activities to accommodate and reflect new workflows and procedures. Implementation of measures to integrate newsrooms has started across all six PSMs. Radio Television of Serbia encouraged by the projects activity in this field has started the newsroom integration process becoming the second PSM in the region with integrated newsroom with journalists working for TV radio and online news sitting together. BHRT which has an integrated newsroom completed the preparations and launched the redesigned website and application in line with a new Digital First mission. RTCG staff were trained on how to include the newsroom integration into the ongoing digitalization process and first steps in the editorialproduction newsroom integration.Journalists have been trained to take up new newsroom positions required by the process of the integrations.29 journalists have been trained in mobile journalism and multiplatform production with 12 mobile journalism stories produced and published. 12 journalists have been trained in social media platformspecific production12 journalists have been trained in data visualisation

description.narrative: OC5: MostPSMs are embarking on management reforms based on needs analyses, following reform designs and corresponding capacity building programmes. At least 2 PSBs in the region are implementing national road maps on management reforms n or violenceeform

title.narrative: OC5

description.narrative: Number of needs analysis and management reform strategy documents drafted and implemented, including proposed capacitybuilding activities

comment.narrative: All six PSMs have agreed management reform plans had them approved and are beginning to implement them. Five countryspecific Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents were developed and agreed with PSM senior management. RTS Serbia had already produced one before the start of this activityCorporate strategies were developed for North Macedonian and Bosnian public broadcasters. These documents were developed in close cooperation with broadcasters senior management structures and approved by relevant PSM governing bodies. These broadcasters have continued to implement the strategic plans and the implementation of the respective road map for management changes document. The draft corporate strategy was developed for Albanian public broadcaster RTSH but after the change at the top management level it is awaiting approval.Internal skills and capacities strengthened in five broadcasters through tailormade workshops on programming strategies financial planning HR practice business planning and public diplomacy strategy development. Regional strategic document Recommendations for Improvement of Minority Reporting in the Western Balkans Public Broadcasters agreed upon and adopted by five PSMs at the regional conference in Novi Sad April 2022In response to COVID challenges 6 Management reforms Optimization of budgets and Updated Road maps were developed with each broadcaster

description.narrative: Number of regulatory bodies participating in masterclasses and their commitment to conduct audience surveys in the future along the agreed guidelines

comment.narrative: 2017Audience research is mostly conducted by agencies on a commercial basis and PSMs complain that it is skewed in favour of private broadcasters

The assumption behind this outcome was rejected by the regulatory authorities at the outset of the project as they did not have the resources or willingness to develop a regional approach. So the project in cooperation with DG Near worked on building the national capacity to develop understand and use audience measurement tools and data to improve quality and enhance accountability.Awareness and knowledge raised on use of audience measurement across six PSMs via regional workshops and national consultancies. 50 management editorial and technical staff members from six PSMs were trained and presented with methods to improve and enhance their current audience measurement systems. Representatives of the regulatory bodies have been included in the discussion and presented with the possibilities of their involvement in this field. PSMs have agreed a set of steps to introduce andor enhance use of audience measurement systems

description.narrative: Factchecking teams/responsibility created.Training of journalists in factchecking completedCapacity built by training staff as trainers to integrate factchecking in to editorial practicesFake News alerts published

comment.narrative: 2022Factchecking teams established in at least 3 PSMsPSMs engaged actively in fact checking especially ahead during and after the major events elections political events etc.At least 3 PSMs actively and regularly contributing to the fake news alert listInhouse training of staff in factchecking is being implemented and factchecking procedures incorporated in newsroom practice.

The results are only partially achieved. While journalists have been trained in all six PSMs and there is a network established to share regional disinformation alerts across PSMs more management buyin and daily integration of factchecking in editorial processes is needed.30 news desk journalists across six PSMs were trained on how to identify analyze and check facts from the statements of public officials politicians and other relevant authority figures determine the method and possible sources for checking data and identify the tools and practices for verification of material collected from social media. A methodology for creating a misinformation Alert List was agreed including the format content and categories of informationMisDisinformation Alert List created and shared online among trained journalists.

description.narrative: OC8: Participating PSMs have begun coproducing programmes and news, based on investigations, with the projects support in training, coaching and editorial development les domaines cibls par la coopration Cameroun / UE

title.narrative: OC8

description.narrative: Investigative news reports and programmes produced and distributedImproved highquality, indepth coverage of broader range of public interest issues.

comment.narrative: 2017As a result of the EUfunded project implemented by the EBU RTCG set up an investigative unit and its outputs were rebroadcast on HRT in Croatia. RTK has a regular investigative programme Jeta na Kosoves which is outsourced and produced by BIRN Kosovo

As a result of the mentoring at least four news reports per PSM are based on multiple sources and look beyond the official version of events. Mentors also shape at least four proposed programmes e.g. shortform documentaries or consumer watchdog shows which have investigative elementsFour regional coproductions are planned and themes agreed. RTK and RTCG are likely to take an active role in this process2021Journalists trained in indepth coverage of public interest issuesNewsroom managers coached on developing alternative organisational structureworkflow to handle future crises2022At least two long form documentary investigative pieces are produced focusing on environment organized crime or corruptionPSM indepth coverage of public interest issues increases.

36 TV stories with investigative elements have been produced and disseminated according to a jointly agreed plan among broadcasters and broadcast throughout the six countries.The practice of crossborder coproduction was established among six broadcasters. Two crossborder coproduction teams were established each comprising journalists from three national public broadcasters.Two longerform investigative documentaries on transborder issues were produced. 14 investigative journalists from six PSMs have been trained and had their skills and capacity for investigative reporting raised.The Inhouse skills and capacity of 32 journalists producers and editors for producing indepth highquality public interest content has been increased Editorial procedures for investigative reporting unit developed and approved for the Montenegrin public broadcaster including investigative unit which will coordinate investigative work among Radio TV and the news portal. Memorandum of understanding of joint work on the investigative program content development among BiHRT and BIRN within the project agreed and signed.

description.narrative: Investigative news reports and programmes produced and distributedImproved highquality, indepth coverage of broader range of public interest issues.

comment.narrative: 2017As a result of the EUfunded project implemented by the EBU RTCG set up an investigative unit and its outputs were rebroadcast on HRT in Croatia. RTK has a regular investigative programme Jeta na Kosoves which is outsourced and produced by BIRN Kosovo

As a result of the mentoring at least four news reports per PSM are based on multiple sources and look beyond the official version of events. Mentors also shape at least four proposed programmes e.g. shortform documentaries or consumer watchdog shows which have investigative elementsFour regional coproductions are planned and themes agreed. RTK and RTCG are likely to take an active role in this process2021Journalists trained in indepth coverage of public interest issuesNewsroom managers coached on developing alternative organisational structureworkflow to handle future crises2022At least two long form documentary investigative pieces are produced focusing on environment organized crime or corruptionPSM indepth coverage of public interest issues increases.

36 TV stories with investigative elements have been produced and disseminated according to a jointly agreed plan among broadcasters and broadcast throughout the six countries.The practice of crossborder coproduction was established among six broadcasters. Two crossborder coproduction teams were established each comprising journalists from three national public broadcasters.Two longerform investigative documentaries on transborder issues were produced. 14 investigative journalists from six PSMs have been trained and had their skills and capacity for investigative reporting raised.The Inhouse skills and capacity of 32 journalists producers and editors for producing indepth highquality public interest content has been increased Editorial procedures for investigative reporting unit developed and approved for the Montenegrin public broadcaster including investigative unit which will coordinate investigative work among Radio TV and the news portal. Memorandum of understanding of joint work on the investigative program content development among BiHRT and BIRN within the project agreed and signed.

title.narrative: OC9: The participating PSMs have started coproducing programmes for children and youth and other agreed topics, with the projects support in training, coaching and editorial development

description.narrative: OC9: The participating PSMs have started coproducing programmes for children and youth and other agreed topics, with the projects support in training, coaching and editorial development

title.narrative: OC9

description.narrative: Pilot formats and series of children or youth programmes coproduced and distributed

comment.narrative: Initial reports indicate very few childrens and youth programmes are coproduced in region

During the training and coaching cycle programmemakers from each broadcaster produce up to three twominute trailers 2426 in total for childrens and youth shows. These are shared with stakeholders and the best ideas are commissioned by PSMs. If funding can be secured at least one pilot is commissioned by each broadcaster and up to three coproductions between PSMs are planned2021Staff trained in production techniquesSeries produced2022After the series is broadcast in host country all PSMs will offers series for the exchange

45 childrens programmes staff members from all six PSMS have been trained on how to develop a full program series for children and youth from screenplay writing and budget preparation to the final phases of editing graphic design and postproduction.48 trailers for children or youth program on different media platforms TV website and social media platforms were produced by six PSMsFive PSMs have produced and broadcast a 12episode series of a program for children and youthoRTCG The show Extraordinary Stories deals with topics of human feelings and relationships through objects plants and animals which have human qualities humanity selfishness sociability naivety fears and loneliness.oRTS Singing picture book is a program for preschool children a combination of childrens songs and animation. A simple animation that illustrates the content of songs makes them more attractive to children and invites them into a fascinating world of animation.oBHRT First time is a program for teenagers hosted by a young and wellknown male journalist who is very close to the age group with his energy and vibe. In every episode he is on a mission confronting a challenge for the first time in his life. oRTSH I have a secret is a series focused on one of the most important components of a childs life being secure. The aim is to listen and understand the meaning of keeping secrets and all the consequences they bring. oRTK Sexual education provides the opportunity for teenagers to explore and define their individual values as well as values of their families and communities and includes a wide variety of sexrelated topics such as hormones and puberty contraception pregnancy LGBTQ etc. Five PSMs have exchanged the series in a regional cooperation for broadcast in each country.Childrens program producers have agreed to launch the Balkans kids brand to promote each others work by using the joint hashtag balkankids for all the seriesrelated social media content. httpswww.youtube.comwatchv9f6FkRhuS2kt2sThe Project significantly increased the awareness of PSM managements of the importance of programs for children and youth and reaching younger audiences.

comment.narrative: Only three PSMs Albania Bosnia and Herzegovina Serbia have part of their budget funded through fees

In those countries where PSMs are statefunded raised awareness among lawmakers and politicians about EU standards and best practices in funding modelsIn countries which are moving towards the core principles support is given to facilitate these processes

A combination of the impact of Covid and political instability across the region meant that there was insufficient political will or process to deliver on the agreed principles. PSMs have committed to it and a plan of action and proposed legislative changes have been produced. Some are awaiting implementation some are still awaiting introduction in the parliaments.

comment.narrative: Only three PSMs Albania Bosnia and Herzegovina Serbia have part of their budget funded through fees

In those countries where PSMs are statefunded raised awareness among lawmakers and politicians about EU standards and best practices in funding modelsIn countries which are moving towards the core principles support is given to facilitate these processes

A combination of the impact of Covid and political instability across the region meant that there was insufficient political will or process to deliver on the agreed principles. PSMs have committed to it and a plan of action and proposed legislative changes have been produced. Some are awaiting implementation some are still awaiting introduction in the parliaments.

title.narrative: OP1.4 Progress is made towards achieving adequate, stable funding in postCovid situation.

description.narrative: OP1.4 Progress is made towards achieving adequate, stable funding in postCovid situation.

title.narrative: OP1.4

description.narrative: Annual assessment reports on funding monitor changes

comment.narrative: No annual assessment published at
assessment reports published

Frequent political changes and snap elections induced changes in the project stakeholders structure in many countries notably so in Montenegro and Kosovo making continuity of work hard and progress slower. Also in some countries a lack of sincere political will to lift control over public broadcasters is registered. That challenge was mitigated to some extent by maintaining continuous contact with stakeholders from all political ranks various members of parliaments and PSM management during the assistance and mentoring process.Serious financial consequences as a result of the Covid19 pandemic often challenged already weak existing PSM funding models exacerbated implementation difficulties and led to some calls for even more restricted funding. Project experts acted as public advocates and in several cases were able to use project activities as a platform to appeal to governments and legislators to ensure sufficient and stable PSM funding.

comment.narrative: Common Principles on PSM GovernanceSupervision in the Western Balkans agreed upon and adopted by project stakeholders at the Belgrade regional conference February 2020.Six regional debates organized and public discussion initiated with more than 180 stakeholders directly involved.National assessment groups set up and countryspecific reports produced with concrete recommendations for PSM governance Awareness raised among stakeholders on the necessity to clearly separate PSM powers among management and governing structures. Regionally agreed common principles documents for PSM funding and governance formally accepted by the EUMontenegro Stabilisation and Association Parliamentary Committee SAPC held in Podgorica in February 2020. Significant publicity produced and public advocacy programs conducted in 6 countries during the project implementation period. Regional principles for PSM governance in Western Balkans are serving as a reference point for public discussion and ongoing legislative deliberations in six Western Balkans countries.

description.narrative: Assessment reports monitor changes

comment.narrative: Common Principles on PSM GovernanceSupervision in the Western Balkans agreed upon and adopted by project stakeholders at the Belgrade regional conference February 2020.Six regional debates organized and public discussion initiated with more than 180 stakeholders directly involved.National assessment groups set up and countryspecific reports produced with concrete recommendations for PSM governance Awareness raised among stakeholders on the necessity to clearly separate PSM powers among management and governing structures. Regionally agreed common principles documents for PSM funding and governance formally accepted by the EUMontenegro Stabilisation and Association Parliamentary Committee SAPC held in Podgorica in February 2020. Significant publicity produced and public advocacy programs conducted in 6 countries during the project implementation period. Regional principles for PSM governance in Western Balkans are serving as a reference point for public discussion and ongoing legislative deliberations in six Western Balkans countries.

title.narrative: OP2.5

description.narrative: Supervisory bodies demonstrate improved knowledge of application of common principles on governance

comment.narrative: A series of project experts field visits to the six Western Balkans countries was conducted. A countryspecific Analysis of PSM Governance Situation was produced covering each of the six countries. The experts met with 1020 relevant stakeholders in each country. National debates on public service media governance were organized in each of the six Western Balkan countries October 2018 February 2020 with an average of 30 delegates participating in each country.A study visit to the Austrian public broadcaster ORF was organized for 14 stakeholders from six countries who gained direct insight into the governance model of Austrian public broadcaster Vienna April 2019 A study visit to the Slovenian public broadcaster RTV SLO was organized for 18 key stakeholders from six countries to gain direct insight into the governance model of the Slovenian public broadcaster Ljubljana June 2019 Following consultations common regional principles on PSM governance were produced.The Western Balkans conference on regionally agreed principles for PSM governance was organized Belgrade Jan. 2020 and attended by more than 40 stakeholders. The conference adopted the regionally agreed principles for PSM governance.Six national assessment groups were constituted and joint work was conducted to define the level of alignment of PSM governance practices with regionally agreed PSM governance principles Working with national assessment groups three PSM governance assessment reports were produced for each country Initial reports midterm reports and final PSM governance assessment reports which contain recommendations for changes of existing legislation and practice. Organised a regional workshop which brought together 30 representatives of the responsible Parliamentary committees and all six PSM supervisory bodies in the Western Balkans with the involvement of the Council of Europe to reinforce the clear separation of roles and responsibilities between supervisory and managerial powers in public media Podgorica March 2022The organization of a regional conference Presentation of the Assessment Reports on Public Service Media Funding and Governance in the Western Balkans Countries Podgorica July 2022

comment.narrative: Five out of six PSMs have outdated editorial guidelines. Only two have a working complaints mechanism and one RTSH has a longterm strategy

Code of conduct for editorial guidelines and complaints mechanisms as well as synopsis for longterm strategy agreed by key stakeholders. Majority of PSMs have implemented strategies and editorial guidelinesImproved implementation of guidelines development of complaints mechanisms where they do not exist and improved promotion where they do

More than 100 journalists and editorial staff gained better knowledge of the content of its PSMs editorial guidelines and the way of its effective implementation and daily usage in practice. All six PSMs agreed to and signed the joint framework for editorial and ethical guidelines and the list of recommendations for improved implementation. June 2019. With the declaration all 6 PSMs committed themselves tooTo adopt editorial guidelines that would ideally include and detail PSM values ethical principles issues practices and proceduresoTo update periodically these editorial guidelines in order to address emerging issues or dilemmasoTo do so drawing up and updating in consultation with journalists to ease appropriation of common standards in the newsroomoTo organize regular newsroom meetings and trainings to share ethical problems behavior and standardsoTo mentor young journalists to generalize ethical behavioroTo capitalize in the long term on experienced journalists interested in ethicsoTo develop whenever possible ethical support to journalists such as a head of ethics in the newsroom or a newsombudsman.At RTSH RTK and RTCG journalists developed processes for implementing guidelines in daily activity.BHRT developed updated guidelines as a result of national workshopsAt MRT journalists have been trained on how to implement guidelines in a politically challenging environmentAt RTS a code of conduct for employees and editorial guidelines was developed. The national coaching ensured wider dissemination and ownership of the editorial guidelines by involving both journalistic and editorial staff and using a bottomup approach.

comment.narrative: No existing effective complaints mechanisms.
PSMS have updated editorial guidelinesPSMs have introduced complaints mechanism

Plans have been agreed by all six PSMs in one case it is fully implemented. In others it is a work in progress.Awareness was raised on the need for and effective use of complaints mechanisms and best practices were shared by European media.Tailormade stepbystep road map and timeline for each PSM on introducing complaints mechanisms agreed in each of the six Western Balkans countries.RTCG appointed a new Ombudsperson and the project provided expertise via Ombudsperson of RTV Slovenia to strengthen their work. She gained knowledge of the relations and necessary rules for the relations of Ombudsman with main stakeholders such as editorial offices management board and viewers and listeners.

title.narrative: OP4.1: Strategy and action plan for integrated newsroom

description.narrative: OP4.1: Strategy and action plan for integrated newsroom

title.narrative: OP4.1

description.narrative: Analysis, strategy and action plan produced and implemented where funding and managerial buyin allow

comment.narrative: Only the broadcasters in Bosnia and Herzegovina have taken the first steps towards creating and rolling out an integrated newsroom
Strategy and plan produced and agreed by 5 out of 6 PSMs and implemented by those broadcasters where funding can be allocated

Awareness raised of benefits of and requirements for developing integrated newsrooms as a result of study visit to YLE Finland.News and production staff of all six PSMs have been trained how to better organize daily planning and manage production resources to coordinate news teams across platforms in order to achieve maximum efficiency and improve online output.Six tailored national action plans for setting up integrated newsrooms and multiplatform production and distribution radio television mobile and online have been produced and presented to management. Common to all actions plans is oIdentifying the weaknesses within existing teams and the training needs for journalistsoIntroducing policies which ensure unified approaches and a robust editorial frameworkoIntroducing management activities to accommodate and reflect new workflows and procedures. Implementation of measures to integrate newsrooms has started across all six PSMs. Radio Television of Serbia encouraged by the projects activity in this field has started the newsroom integration process becoming the second PSM in the region with integrated newsroom with journalists working for TV radio and online news sitting together. BHRT which has an integrated newsroom completed the preparations and launched the redesigned website and application in line with a new Digital First mission. RTCG staff were trained on how to include the newsroom integration into the ongoing digitalization process and first steps in the editorialproduction newsroom integration.Journalists have been trained to take up new newsroom positions required by the process of the integrations.29 journalists have been trained in mobile journalism and multiplatform production with 12 mobile journalism stories produced and published. 12 journalists have been trained in social media platformspecific production12 journalists have been trained in data visualisation

Awareness raised of benefits of and requirements for developing integrated newsrooms as a result of study visit to YLE Finland.News and production staff of all six PSMs have been trained how to better organize daily planning and manage production resources to coordinate news teams across platforms in order to achieve maximum efficiency and improve online output.Six tailored national action plans for setting up integrated newsrooms and multiplatform production and distribution radio television mobile and online have been produced and presented to management. Common to all actions plans is oIdentifying the weaknesses within existing teams and the training needs for journalistsoIntroducing policies which ensure unified approaches and a robust editorial frameworkoIntroducing management activities to accommodate and reflect new workflows and procedures. Implementation of measures to integrate newsrooms has started across all six PSMs. Radio Television of Serbia encouraged by the projects activity in this field has started the newsroom integration process becoming the second PSM in the region with integrated newsroom with journalists working for TV radio and online news sitting together. BHRT which has an integrated newsroom completed the preparations and launched the redesigned website and application in line with a new Digital First mission. RTCG staff were trained on how to include the newsroom integration into the ongoing digitalization process and first steps in the editorialproduction newsroom integration.Journalists have been trained to take up new newsroom positions required by the process of the integrations.29 journalists have been trained in mobile journalism and multiplatform production with 12 mobile journalism stories produced and published. 12 journalists have been trained in social media platformspecific production12 journalists have been trained in data visualisation

Five countryspecific Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents were developed and agreed with PSM senior management.Corporate strategies were developed for North Macedonian and Bosnian public broadcasters. These documents were developed in close cooperation with broadcasters senior management structures and approved by relevant PSM governing bodies. These broadcasters have continued to implement the strategic plans and the implementation of the respective road map for management changes document. The draft corporate strategy was developed for Albanian public broadcaster RTSH but after the change at the top management level it is awaiting approval.Internal skills and capacities strengthened in five broadcasters through tailormade workshops on programming strategies financial planning HR practice business planning and public diplomacy strategy development. Regional strategic document Recommendations for Improvement of Minority Reporting in the Western Balkans Public Broadcasters agreed upon and adopted by five PSMs at the regional conference in Novi Sad April 2022In response to COVID challenges 6 documents produced Management reforms Optimization of budgets and Updated Road maps for each broadcaster

comment.narrative: Updated road mapsOrganograms PSM policiesprocedures setting out management roles and responsibilities

Five countryspecific Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents were developed and agreed with PSM senior management.Corporate strategies were developed for North Macedonian and Bosnian public broadcasters. These documents were developed in close cooperation with broadcasters senior management structures and approved by relevant PSM governing bodies. These broadcasters have continued to implement the strategic plans and the implementation of the respective road map for management changes document. The draft corporate strategy was developed for Albanian public broadcaster RTSH but after the change at the top management level it is awaiting approval.Internal skills and capacities strengthened in five broadcasters through tailormade workshops on programming strategies financial planning HR practice business planning and public diplomacy strategy development. Regional strategic document Recommendations for Improvement of Minority Reporting in the Western Balkans Public Broadcasters agreed upon and adopted by five PSMs at the regional conference in Novi Sad April 2022In response to COVID challenges 6 documents produced Management reforms Optimization of budgets and Updated Road maps for each broadcasterActivities performedExperts conducted field visits to six Western Balkans countries to develop baseline assessment analysis of needs for management reforms in the individual broadcasters engaging approx. 25 interviewees in each PSM to identify strengths and weaknesses in the current structure.Produced and published Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents for five PSMs in close cooperation with broadcasters management.Reviewed and updated Road Maps for management reform documents in particular in responding to COVIDrelated challenges.Agreeing on a series of tailormade training programmes formats and assistance plans in close cooperation with broadcasters. More than 150 midmanagement PSMs staff consulted during the consultants field visits.Organized and implemented six national inhouse training workshops on HR strategies and leadership for 18 seniormiddle managersOrganized and implemented a series of online regional training workshops for 10 middle managers on planning and budgetingOrganized programming strategy training for 5 PSMs.Organized regional training workshop on online analytics to enable managers to better understand their audience its movement and needs and management and planning practices.Organized a regional conference to improve PSM reporting on minorities in Novi Sad April 2022 attended by 40 participants. Before the event the project experts visited broadcasters in the region to assess the situation and conducted a survey to define the state of affairs about minority reporting

comment.narrative: Updated road mapsOrganograms PSM policiesprocedures setting out management roles and responsibilities

Five countryspecific Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents were developed and agreed with PSM senior management.Corporate strategies were developed for North Macedonian and Bosnian public broadcasters. These documents were developed in close cooperation with broadcasters senior management structures and approved by relevant PSM governing bodies. These broadcasters have continued to implement the strategic plans and the implementation of the respective road map for management changes document. The draft corporate strategy was developed for Albanian public broadcaster RTSH but after the change at the top management level it is awaiting approval.Internal skills and capacities strengthened in five broadcasters through tailormade workshops on programming strategies financial planning HR practice business planning and public diplomacy strategy development. Regional strategic document Recommendations for Improvement of Minority Reporting in the Western Balkans Public Broadcasters agreed upon and adopted by five PSMs at the regional conference in Novi Sad April 2022In response to COVID challenges 6 documents produced Management reforms Optimization of budgets and Updated Road maps for each broadcasterActivities performedExperts conducted field visits to six Western Balkans countries to develop baseline assessment analysis of needs for management reforms in the individual broadcasters engaging approx. 25 interviewees in each PSM to identify strengths and weaknesses in the current structure.Produced and published Needs Assessment Survey for Management Reforms with Road Map documents for five PSMs in close cooperation with broadcasters management.Reviewed and updated Road Maps for management reform documents in particular in responding to COVIDrelated challenges.Agreeing on a series of tailormade training programmes formats and assistance plans in close cooperation with broadcasters. More than 150 midmanagement PSMs staff consulted during the consultants field visits.Organized and implemented six national inhouse training workshops on HR strategies and leadership for 18 seniormiddle managersOrganized and implemented a series of online regional training workshops for 10 middle managers on planning and budgetingOrganized programming strategy training for 5 PSMs.Organized regional training workshop on online analytics to enable managers to better understand their audience its movement and needs and management and planning practices.Organized a regional conference to improve PSM reporting on minorities in Novi Sad April 2022 attended by 40 participants. Before the event the project experts visited broadcasters in the region to assess the situation and conducted a survey to define the state of affairs about minority reporting

title.narrative: OP6.1: Joint guidelines for production of audience researchceses

description.narrative: OP6.1: Joint guidelines for production of audience research ce.

title.narrative: OP6.1

description.narrative: Guidelines developed

comment.narrative: The assessment of the audience measurement for PSM in the Western Balkans clearly indicated that the initial proposal of the activity aimed only at regulatory bodies had to be modified as Regulatory Bodies were not interested in carrying out audience surveys themselves. Moreover most regulatory bodies do not have the financial capacities or human resources to commission or carry out audience measurement themselves but can be a driving force to bring industry stakeholders together. At the project Inception meeting and the first stakeholders meeting in Tirana in 2018 the regulatory bodies made it clear they could not carry out this work and it was agreed with DG Near in the extension of the project that the activity should focus on developing the better use of modern audience measurement tools at each PSM which was done.Awareness and knowledge raised on use of audience measurement across six PSMs via regional workshops and national consultancies. 50 management editorial and technical staff members from six PSMs were trained and presented with methods to improve and enhance their current audience measurement systems. Representatives of the regulatory bodies have been included in the discussion and presented with the possibilities of their involvement in this field. PSMs have agreed a set of steps to introduce andor enhance use of audience measurement systems

description.narrative: Topics identifiedResearch conductedNews reports producedProgrammes enhanced

comment.narrative: At least four of the PSMs agree to produce and broadcast a total of 24 news reports with strong investigative elements as well as enhanced programmes on issues such as consumer rights. At least two PSMs plan regional coproductions

36 TV stories with investigative elements have been produced and disseminated according to a jointly agreed plan among broadcasters and broadcast throughout the six countries.The practice of crossborder coproduction was established among six broadcasters. Two crossborder coproduction teams were established each comprising journalists from three national public broadcasters.Two longerform investigative documentaries on transborder issues were produced. 14 investigative journalists from six PSMs have been trained and had their skills and capacity for investigative reporting raised.The Inhouse skills and capacity of 32 journalists producers and editors for producing indepth highquality public interest content has been increased Editorial procedures for investigative reporting unit developed and approved for the Montenegrin public broadcaster including investigative unit which will coordinate investigative work among Radio TV and the news portal. Memorandum of understanding of joint work on the investigative program content development among BiHRT and BIRN within the project agreed and signed.

comment.narrative: At least four of the PSMs agree to produce and broadcast a total of 24 news reports with strong investigative elements as well as enhanced programmes on issues such as consumer rights. At least two PSMs plan regional coproductions

36 TV stories with investigative elements have been produced and disseminated according to a jointly agreed plan among broadcasters and broadcast throughout the six countries.The practice of crossborder coproduction was established among six broadcasters. Two crossborder coproduction teams were established each comprising journalists from three national public broadcasters.Two longerform investigative documentaries on transborder issues were produced. 14 investigative journalists from six PSMs have been trained and had their skills and capacity for investigative reporting raised.The Inhouse skills and capacity of 32 journalists producers and editors for producing indepth highquality public interest content has been increased Editorial procedures for investigative reporting unit developed and approved for the Montenegrin public broadcaster including investigative unit which will coordinate investigative work among Radio TV and the news portal. Memorandum of understanding of joint work on the investigative program content development among BiHRT and BIRN within the project agreed and signed.

title.narrative: OP8.1: A minimum of 24 news reports with investigative elements are produced in collaboration with mentors; a further 24 programmes focusing on issues such as consumers rights are shaped and enhanced though the project. description.narrative: OP8.3: Journalists/managers trained in developing skills and processes to deliver indepth quality public interest journalism

title.narrative: OP 8.3

description.narrative: Increase in number of journalists producing quality, indepth public interest journalism

comment.narrative: With an increasing number of health environmental financial and economic crises journalists and managers lack training in key public interest content and organisational processes to achieve more sustained and quality content and workflows

Up to 24 journalists trained in developing indepth public interest content particularly in crisis coverage.Up to 12 managers trained in adapting organisational structuresworkflows to handle crises and enable more indepth coverage of public interest issues.
The Inhouse skills and capacity of 32 journalists producers and editors for producing indepth highquality public interest content has been increased

Threeday regional investigative reporting training for 13 journalists dedicated to investigative reporting from the six news departments. Journalists trained for investigative journalism and coached in a process of developing programme topics Belgrade October 1214 12 members of production teams across six PSMs received online training and mentoring sessions and advice on practical matters concerning producing reports and programmes based on investigative journalism. Online Nov 2018 Jan 2019Coaching for 14 investigative journalists in research preparation and production online Feb 2019 June 2019Organizing threeday regional meeting to launch investigative reports and agree on a dissemination plan among the editors involved in the investigative reporting program Podgorica January 2019 Support provided to six PSMs to identify journalists editors and producers who will take part in the crossborder investigative teams September 2020 January 2021Creation of two crossborder investigative teams each comprising of journalists from 3 PSMs Sept.2020 Jan.2021Support provided to two crossborder documentary coproductions. Providing crossborder investigative teams with onthejob mentoring production assistance and dissemination support for two longform documentary investigative piecesMentoring of the crossborder teams through webinars held monthly based on needs. title.narrative: Growth in audience ratings and market share for PSMIncrease in the number of respondents to audience surveys who confirm that they have noticed qualitative improvements in PSM outputs and reduced evidence of progovernment bias

description.narrative: Growth in audience ratings and market share for PSMIncrease in the number of respondents to audience surveys who confirm that they have noticed qualitative improvements in PSM outputs and reduced evidence of progovernment bias

comment.narrative: Audiences agree that they have greater trust in PSM outputs than in those of private media particularly for news content and programming for children and young peopleAll PSMs are implementing agreed changes in funding governance managements andor contentTrust in PSMs is increased across a range of content

During the Covid crisis there was evidence of a greater reliance on public service media for necessary information and PSMs extended the range of programmes available including providing greater emphasis on education. As a result there was a growth recorded in public trust but it is fragile as political interference remains a significant factor in undermining the credibility of PSMs in the region.
